Learn how to utilize Terraform modules from a different repository through GitHub Actions.

Owen Olwethu Phakade
3 min read
·
Aug 3, 2023

--

I enjoy dedicating a significant portion of my time to experimenting with Terraform. A major focus is on creating custom Terraform modules that I access from external repositories/workflows. While referencing a module in my local development environment works seamlessly, challenges arise when running the declared module in a continuous integration (CI) environment.

When executing the `terraform init` command, Terraform imports a module from its source. If the module is stored in a GitHub repository (which is the case for all my modules), your computer establishes an SSH connection with the GitHub repo to retrieve the module, provided you are already authenticated with GitHub. However, reproducing the same process on GitHub Actions might fail due to authentication issues. Yep, we need to authenticate the Github action runner.

The most effective way to Authenticate a GITHUB action runner.

  1. On your terminal create a SSH key pair.
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "your_email@example.com"

2. Copy the Public key.

cat $HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
#Select and copy the contents of id_ed25519.pub

3. Head on over to your GitHub settings and paste the public key.

4. Copy the Private key.

cat $HOME/.ssh/id_ed25519
#Select and copy the contents of id_ed25519.pub

5. Head on over to your GitHub repo settings > settings/secrets/actions/. Give it a unique name and paste in the private key.

6. Finally, go to your GitHub action workflow file, add the following Action then run your workflow. Note — The action should be added before any Terraform initialization step.

- name: Set up SSH agent
      uses: webfactory/ssh-agent@v0.5.4
      with:
        ssh-private-key: ${{ secrets.<your-private-key> }}

Conclusion

I discovered this to be the most flexible and straightforward method for authentication and utilization of Terraform modules located in different repositories. This approach eliminates the need to manage deploy keys or using bash scripts to configure git credentials. I hope this information proves beneficial to you. Happy coding!
